newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Green candidate in Stuttgart mayor race.
newsitem.headline: German Green candidate in Stuttgart mayor race.

text.p: A candidate from the Greens party was fighting a close run-off election race on Sunday for the mayor of Stuttgart, hoping to become the first mayor from the environmentalist party to govern a major German city.

Rezzo Schlauch received a surprisingly strong 30.6 percent of the vote in the first round on October 20 and came in second just behind the Christian Democratic (CDU) candidate Wolfgang Schuster, who had 35.2 percent.
Schlauch's second place finish in the first round knocked out the Social Democratic (SPD) candidate Rainer Brechtgen who was in third place with 22.6 percent.
With 600,000 citizens, Stuttgart, state capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and home to the huge industrial group, Daimler-Benz AG, is Germany's seventh largest city.
The race is to find a successor for Manfred Rommel of the CDU who is retiring after 22 years in the post.
A survey by the Stuttgarter Zeitung newspaper gave Schuster 41 percent of the vote compared to 36 percent for Schlauch.
But this picture could be distorted because of the late wildcard entry into the run-off of Joachim Becker (SPD), who is mayor of the suburban town of Pforzheim.
